gaps.sentence: Rarely ___ we seen such dedication from a new recruit.
gaps.explanation: 'Rarely have we seen' — inversion with present perfect, experience up to now.

gaps.sentence: At no point ___ the passengers instructed to stay seated.
gaps.explanation: 'At no point were the passengers instructed …' — inverted passive.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets expensive, but they were also sold out.
gaps.explanation: Not only were the tickets… — inversion with 'be' needs no auxiliary.

gaps.sentence: Hardly had we left the house ___ it started to pour.
gaps.explanation: Hardly … when — fixed pair; 'than' belongs to 'no sooner'.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the chances of success be improved by patience.
gaps.explanation: Little will the chances be improved… — inversion with future.

gaps.sentence: ___ the committee reach a decision, we cannot proceed.
gaps.explanation: Fronting 'Until…' emphasises the condition blocking progress.

gaps.sentence: Not since the 1990s ___ unemployment been so low.
gaps.explanation: Not since X has Y happened — present perfect inversion.

gaps.sentence: Only after the interview ___ I realise how nervous I had been.
gaps.explanation: Only after X did I realise… — inversion.
